result.title: Cascading Bandits with Noisy Observations: Algorithms and Regret Bounds
result.summary: We propose a novel stochastic cascading bandit setup where probing an ordered shortlist of $K$ out of $L$ arms incurs position-dependent costs, and the learner observes only noisy feedback regarding each arm's true output. We identify a sub-class of noise models for which the optimal shortlist can be found by sorting arms according to a per-arm score: such a score exists for both selection and ordering when the channel has no false positives, and for ordering alone (but not selection) when measurements are costless; however in general neither selection nor ordering is separable once noise and cost are both present. For the case where both selection and ordering scores exist, we provide a UCB-based algorithm with $O((L-K)\log T)$ instance-dependent regret over a time horizon $T$, which matches an algorithm-agnostic lower bound (up to constant factors). For the more challenging scenario where scores don't exist, we develop a new algorithmic template, DP-UCB, that embeds optimism directly inside an exact dynamic program, yielding $O\big(LK\log T\big)$ regret. Finally, we validate our theoretical results through extensive numerical evaluations and simulations over both synthetic and real-world datasets.

AI.brief_summary: 研究带噪声观测的级联 bandit：探测由 L 个臂中选出并排序的 K 元候选列表会产生位置相关成本，学习器只得到关于各臂真实输出的噪声反馈；论文刻画了可按单臂分数排序的最优列表何时存在，并分别给出 UCB 与嵌入乐观性的 DP-UCB 算法及相应 regret 界。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「位置成本 + 噪声反馈下选择与排序证据条目」的决策模型，可能为视觉证据筛选、LOOK/THINK 的收益-成本权衡与获取顺序设计提供形式化参照，可供核查其可分性条件是否刻画实际观测噪声情形。
